reason: The cited evidence shows that SRO can be induced by processing (E3) and that ordering raises activation barriers for dislocation motion (E3, E4), but none of the passages directly demonstrate that SRO increases atomic diffusion barriers, suppresses grain growth, or inhibits phase segregation in Al0.1CrCoFeNi nanoparticles. The key mechanistic link between SRO and diffusion-controlled stability is unsupported by the cited data.
premises: Short-range chemical order (SRO) can be induced in Al0.1CrCoFeNi by intermediate temperature annealing
SRO increases local atomic diffusion barriers by relieving local stress and stabilizing favorable configurations
Increased diffusion barriers suppress grain growth and phase segregation at high temperature
Randomly quenched nanoparticles lack SRO and thus exhibit faster diffusion-driven degradation
The stabilizing effect of SRO diminishes above ~900 °C as thermal energy overcomes ordering-induced barriers
